title: The Lost Blue Feather
markdown:
The sun was just waking up and painting the sky with pretty pinks and soft oranges. Flora the fox cub stretched her little legs. Her fur was the color of honey, and her tail gave a happy wag, swish-swish-swish. Beside her, Bean the bunny wiggled his nose. His long, soft ears twitched. The morning air smelled sweet like soft earth and sleepy flowers.

"Oh, look, Flora!" whispered Bean. He pointed with a tiny pink paw.

There, tucked in the green leaves, was a feather. It was the prettiest feather they had ever seen! It was very, very blue, like the bright sky. And it sparkled just a little, like sunshine peeking out.

"It's so pretty," said Flora. Her tail gave a slow, thoughtful swish. She looked closer with her bright eyes. "But who does it belong to?"

Bean twitched his ears. One flopped down a little. "Hmm," he mumbled. His little pink nose wiggled as he thought. "I think... I think it might be Ruby the robin's feather!"

"Ruby!" said Flora. Her tail thumped softly on the ground. "She has such lovely blue feathers, doesn't she? So bright!"

"She does!" agreed Bean. "And she always sings the nicest songs. Maybe she misses her feather. Maybe she can't sing her best songs without it."

Ruby the robin lived a little way in the woods. The leaves there were thick, like a big green hug.

"We must take it back to her," said Flora. Her voice was kind. Her tail gave a determined swish. "She'll be so happy!"

"But it's so quiet," whispered Bean. He looked at the tall leaves. "We must tiptoe very, very quietly. Like little mice."

So, Flora and Bean started their tiptoe adventure. Flora’s paws made soft little sounds on the moss. Bean’s little feet hardly made a sound at all. Shhh. They peeked through the leaves. Their eyes were wide with gentle wonder. The leaves rustled softly. Tiny dewdrops on the leaves sparkled bright.

"Do you hear anything, Flora?" asked Bean. His ears were perked up high. He held his breath and listened very hard.

Flora listened too. She tilted her head. Her nose twitched. "Only the happy sounds of the morning, Bean," she whispered. "The busy bees buzzing, and the leaves rustling."

And wouldn't you know it, just as they wondered if they were going the right way, they heard a soft, happy sound. "Cheep, cheep!"

"That sounds like Ruby!" chirped Bean. His nose wiggled with delight.

They tiptoed a little further. Their hearts felt light and happy. And there, on a strong branch, was Ruby the robin. She looked a little bit droopy. Her blue tail feathers were not quite neat. She was fluffing one feather that stuck out.

"Ruby!" called Flora softly. Her voice was like a gentle breeze. "We found something for you!"

Ruby tilted her head. Her bright eyes blinked. "Oh, hello, Flora! Hello, Bean! What have you found?" she chirped. Her voice was brighter already.

Flora gently held out the beautiful blue feather. She made sure Ruby could see its sparkle. "We found this! We think it's yours."

Ruby's eyes got wide. She gave a little flutter of her wings. She hopped closer. Her little feet tapped softly on the branch. She gave a little happy trill, like tiny bells. "Oh, my beautiful feather! I was wondering where it had gone! I looked everywhere! Thank you, thank you so much!"

Ruby carefully took the feather in her beak. She held it very gently. Then, with a little wriggle and a proud puff of her chest, she tucked it perfectly back into her tail. It fit just right. She looked so happy, her chest puffed out like a proud balloon.

"Now I can sing my very best songs!" she chirped. And then, she began to sing. It was the sweetest, happiest song. Flora and Bean listened. Their hearts felt warm. They felt as happy as finding a whole field of yummy clover.

"You are such good friends," sang Ruby. "Kind and helpful!"

Flora and Bean giggled. They loved being called good friends. Flora nudged Bean happily with her soft nose.

"Now," said Flora, her tail giving a happy swish, "it's time for us to go home for a warm breakfast. Mama will have made nice warm milk!"

And as they tiptoed back, with the sun now shining brightly, warming their fur and their hearts, Flora and Bean knew that returning a lost feather made their own hearts feel as bright and happy as the feather.
characters: Flora the fox cub, Bean the bunny
